Alpha 1.9.2 (room to play)

  • A bigger seated game view: Casino games now use a larger desktop panel with a persistent Leave button. Slots show larger reels beside a dedicated control column; phone layouts place reels above scrollable, touch-sized controls.
  • Change your next bet: Type a slot stake of 20–500 Gold in steps of 20, or use the ½ / 2× shortcuts. Blackjack bets and poker buy-ins gain the same shortcuts within their existing limits. Submitted wagers stay locked until settled.
  • Manual or Auto: Choose one-spin play or a 50, 100 or custom spin queue from separate tabs. Reels still animate, and Stop cancels only unstarted spins. Saved bonuses and free spins keep their original stake until finished.
  • Gold games stay Gold games: Slot paytables and relative odds are unchanged; larger stakes mean larger possible wins and losses. Card-table limits are unchanged. EP remains a planned cosmetic-only currency; its wallet, exchange, monthly allowance and purchases are not enabled in this release.
  • Recall stays in town: Late snapshots from a previous scene can no longer restore the old dungeon identity or player state after Recall or another scene transition.

Alpha 1.9.1 (the grand casino opens)

  • Enter the grand hall: Click the town casino door and choose Enter Casino to travel to one shared two-storey social zone. Five Gold blackjack tables, real-player poker and four elemental slot machines fill the public floor. Other players share the room and seats. The VIP stair guard says “You must be a VIP to enter”; upstairs games, EP wallets and purchases are not enabled.
  • Fewer clicks, clearer wagers: Slots, blackjack and poker now use direct wager buttons with visible Gold costs, replacing separate review/confirm screens. Double and Split show their extra cost; poker raises and all-ins use the reserved stack. Unchanged polls cannot unlock duplicate clicks, and rejected actions recover without automatic retries.
  • Watch the reels: Symbols spin visibly and reels stop in sequence before winning lines, cascades and result sounds. Reduced-motion preferences remain supported. Outcomes and payouts are still decided and saved by the server.
  • Choose your spin queue: Auto-spin offers 50, 100 or a custom 1–1000 spins, with the maximum total stakes shown before starting. One settled, animated spin runs at a time; saved free spins keep their original stake and count toward the queue. Stop cancels unstarted spins. Leaving, hiding the game, connection trouble, insufficient Gold or a bonus choice stops the queue; it never resumes automatically after reconnect.
  • A place to linger: The shared hall has its own floor, map, lounges and guarded balcony, plus safe-zone recovery and a return-to-town exit. Reconnect restores the shared scene; saved positions inside the old town facade relocate safely outside.
  • After the Dark King: Characters who have completed the main story can read Ilyra’s optional A Letter Without a Throne conversation and new Mara/Selen topics. Help’s Your Next Adventure explains the existing optional story, events, dailies, raid caches and seasons without adding a mandatory grind.

Alpha 1.9.0 (a world that stays interesting)

  • The elements call for help: Rotating disturbances appear along the Earth, Water, Fire and Air roads. Hold Orun’s central ward, follow Tidestar’s answering runes, vent the Ember Crown’s outer ring, or keep moving with Skyglass’s updraft. Nearby adventurers share three defended waves and a Fracturekeeper encounter. World rings, a map marker and a collapsible nearby objective explain the fight.
  • A calmer road afterward: Completing an encounter suppresses nearby elemental hazards for five minutes. The ten-minute rotation includes advance warning and a bounded encounter window; abandoned event enemies expire instead of becoming permanent respawns. Normal enemy loot and party experience apply, without another mandatory daily quest or repeatable completion purse.
  • A real casino in Lanternhold: The stash now sits between the Trading House and the expanded casino, with clear approaches. Walk through the public entrance, approach tables or machines, take a visible seat and use the table-focused view. Leaving restores ordinary movement and camera control.
  • Four elemental slot machines: Orun’s Living Vault roots wilds during free spins; Pyralis’s Ember Forge doubles free-spin wins; Neris’s Returning Tide cascades winning symbols; Aeral’s Unbound Horizon expands wild reels. Each has lore-themed symbols, a sealed story bonus choice, free-spin retriggers, a fixed natural-symbol jackpot, animated results and sound. Ten fixed paylines use a total stake of 20 or 40 normal Gold, with published rules and paytables.
  • Know what you are spending: Paid spins require review and confirmation. Saved free spins retain their original stake and never silently become paid spins. Theme-specific paytables account for bonus mechanics; casino play is entertainment, not a guaranteed source of Gold. Reduced-motion and audio preferences are respected.
  • Fourfold Hold’em with real players: Two to six players can fund a hand of no-limit poker with 5/10 Gold blinds and a confirmed 100–500 Gold buy-in. No house-controlled opponents fill empty seats. Private cards, betting streets, raises, all-ins, main and side pots, tied hands and odd-Gold splits are handled by the server. Unspent stack and winnings return after every hand; a new hand requires a new buy-in confirmation. Solo and multiplayer Lanternhold Blackjack remain available downstairs.
  • Leave without losing track of your Gold: Leaving poker before the deal refunds the buy-in. Leaving after the deal folds a remaining stack; an all-in hand stays eligible. A timed-out turn checks if free or folds to a bet. Funded seats and private hands can recover across reconnects and server restarts. Slot bonuses and free spins belong to their owner even after leaving the machine. Durable receipts prevent accepted debits and payouts from replaying twice.
  • Upstairs is taking shape: A real staircase leads to the two-floor casino’s velvet-and-gold VIP lounge, with floor-aware movement and camera picking. The lounge is walkable, but VIP games are not enabled yet: they await the separately defined special currency. Normal Gold is not an upstairs substitute. Both floors’ full integration and final cross-game stabilization remain part of 1.10.

Alpha 1.8.0 (find your people)

  • Find an adventuring party: The Social window’s Groups tab lists activities, recruitment and preferred roles. Publish a short-lived listing, request a place, review applicants and send an ordinary invitation. Requests never silently join a party; leaders, capacity, level requirements and player availability remain authoritative.
  • Invitations mean consent: Party invitations expire after one minute and can be accepted only once, by their intended recipient, for the original party. Changed leaders, disbanded or full groups, busy players and block/ignore settings are respected.
  • A calendar for your guild: Authorized guild officers can schedule, edit or cancel activities. Members RSVP with attendance and a preferred role; capacity is enforced, schedule changes require renewed confirmation, and events survive reconnects. The roster helps you form an actual party and ready check.
  • Safer social tools: Player rows offer explicit block, ignore and report actions. Reports open a contextual draft for you to review and submit; they never automatically punish another player. Existing block lists and moderation records remain persistent.
  • Take a real seat: Walk into the former town hall and approach a casino chair or machine. The server owns seat occupancy, other players visibly sit beside you, and the camera focuses on the table. Leaving restores normal controls and a safe position; brief reconnects reserve your seat for sixty seconds.
  • Lanternhold Blackjack: Play alone or with up to five other real players against the house dealer using normal Gold. Confirm a 20–500 Gold opening wager, then hit, stand, double or split under the displayed six-deck rules. Shared cards, turn deadlines, balance, extra-wager costs and results are visible in the seated desktop and phone interface.
  • Wagers that survive interruptions: Bets and payouts use saved transaction receipts. Extra wagers require confirmation; delayed requests cannot replay a turn or charge twice. Leaving does not cancel an accepted wager: timed-out hands stand and payouts are saved. Pending funds recover before the affected player can issue another command.
  • Casino rendering: Tables and slot-machine decorations share compatible geometry batches, preventing the complete venue catalog from interrupting world updates.
  • The casino is still growing: This release opens the social space and blackjack. Poker and slot seats are groundwork, not playable games yet. The revised stash layout, full themed games and walkable VIP floor remain upcoming; no premium currency has been invented or substituted with Gold.

Alpha 1.7.0 (the proving grounds)

  • Real practice and ranked teams: Choose separate practice or ranked 1v1 and two-player-party 2v2 queues. Eliminate the whole opposing team to win a round; arenas are first to two. Practice never changes ranked records or grants rewards. No fabricated opponents fill a queue.
  • Fairer matching: Ranked teams seek nearby average ratings, starting within 100 and widening by 50 every thirty seconds, up to 500. Both teams must allow the gap. Queue status shows elapsed time and the actual search window; invalid or changed parties cannot quietly enter, and cancelling either teammate removes the queued team.
  • Builds remain yours: Level, class, equipment and talents still matter. Existing player damage is 65% with a 35%-maximum-health single-hit cap, not hidden stat normalization. Duels recheck nearby living players and reject shared-party opponents or players already in an arena queue.
  • Results with reasons: Team-strength Elo replaces flat rating changes. See your team's score, victory or defeat, exact rating change, Honor and season points, plus any reason rewards were withheld. A tied timeout cancels without selecting an arbitrary winner.
  • Rewards for real competition: Eligible ranked wins award 50 Honor and three season points; losses and forfeits award neither. Only the first three meetings with each opposing player per UTC day change rating or pay rewards, even after team swaps or reconnects. Later matches still record wins and losses. A ranked leaver receives a five-minute queue penalty; their innocent teammate does not.
  • Seasons remembered: Eligible-win tracking begins in 1.7. At quarter end, earn Bronze for ten wins (250 Honor), Silver for twenty-five wins and 1200 rating (600), or Gold for fifty wins and 1500 rating (1200). Only the highest tier pays. Opening or joining the arena settles the completed season once, preserves its record and your Honor, and resets rating to 1000. The panel separates projected medals from settled history.
  • Fresh rounds, safe returns: Rounds begin with fresh combat effects, cooldowns, health and mana. Lingering shields, damage-over-time, summons and projectiles do not carry between rounds or back into the world. Leaving restores pre-match health, mana, position and original cooldown deadlines. Saves during a match retain the original return state, not an arena death or free refill. Well Rested keeps counting down normally.
  • Durable outcomes: Ranked results are recorded before releasing participants, then synchronized to their profiles. Interrupted writes retry the same outcome without paying twice or overwriting a newer result. A pending save is shown honestly; ranked entry waits for synchronization. Season records and opponent limits survive reconnects. Character saves and arena receipts recover independently across server restarts.

Alpha 1.6.0 (the living sanctums)

  • Bosses with different answers: Earth bosses split the ground in a directed fissure; Water locks a surge on its target’s position; Fire erupts in separated pockets; Air closes a storm ring around a safe center. Warning footprints match the actual hit areas, movement advice appears once per attack, and overlapping markers never multiply one attack’s damage.
  • Rootheart’s defended promise: Hold the central ward for eight defended seconds per wave while companions keep corruption outside the outer boundary. Maelin explains why Orun’s sanctuary must shelter people, not imprison them.
  • Tidestar’s carried memories: Bring two memories from the eastern font back to Maelin each wave. A personal tracker reminds carriers to return; death or leaving drops the memory. The crystal heals through remembrance, not forgetting.
  • Ember Crown’s steady hands: Quench three bright vents in order, standing inside each for two uninterrupted seconds. Moving away breaks that channel. Protect your channelers while Maelin remakes Pyralis’s circuit without feeding its old hunger.
  • Skyglass’s shared voice: Pass four wind anchors between different raiders. Two runners can alternate, but one character cannot command every step. Each handoff restores a direction Malachar tried to silence.
  • Finish the whole vigil: Every one of the three waves needs both its ritual task and all attackers defeated. Live and reconnecting players see the task and floor markers, including at Low quality. A wiped or unattended chamber restarts the current task while keeping cleared waves; the tracker no longer tells you to leave before the crystal is restored. Return to Ilyra for your manual quest reward.
  • Prepare, recover, return: The Dungeon Guide explains role-appropriate gear, town recovery, raid ready checks, individual re-entry and the five-minute empty-instance timer. Each raid previews its ritual jobs. Desktop resets now require confirmation, just like the phone route; everyone must leave before a leader discards the run.
  • Weekly rewards without confusion: The Dark King card shows your available, claimed or temporarily unknown cache status and its Monday midnight UTC reset. Claiming a weekly cache does not stop you helping another raid; resetting an instance cannot grant another cache. Malachar’s four Eidolon phases and the earned Chronicle gates remain intact.

Alpha 1.5.0 (loot with purpose)

  • Three loadouts, ready in town: Save named sets of equipped gear, specialization, talents, runes and four skill slots from your bag. Switch while alive in safe town, outside active or recent combat. Missing gear or insufficient bag space rejects the whole swap without moving items. Small landscape phones keep loadout and legacy-recovery disclosures side by side so the bag retains a usable row.
  • Builds with clear costs: Specialization and talent changes show the existing respec price before you confirm. Unchanged builds and rune-only changes are free. Gear, cooldowns, skill points and depleted health or mana are preserved; your last saved or applied skill bar returns on reconnect.
  • Your wardrobe, earned: Open Wardrobe in the character sheet to learn styles and rarity colours from gear you own. Items are not consumed, and learned looks remain after selling them. Apply an earned look to compatible equipped gear, or restore its original appearance. Other players see your choice; combat stats and Forge upgrades stay unchanged.
  • Know what an upgrade buys: Forge tables show current stats, exact gains for each upgrade option, and Shards or Hearts left afterward. Small rounded gains carry forward. Phone-sized controls and live refresh keep decisions readable without closing the Forge.
  • Compare what you really gain: Item comparisons include socketed gem stats and warn when replacing gear loses a set bonus or special effect. Desktop ring and trinket comparisons now use the actual replacement slot, too.
  • Gold with purpose: Ordinary monsters now drop less Gold, elites pay twice the ordinary range, and boss purses remain unchanged. Newly accepted hundred-kill hunts offer twice their previous Gold bonus. Existing Gold, accepted quest quotes, story and weekly rewards, and the Resonance curve are preserved.
  • Casino groundwork: The later physical casino milestones now have explicit wager, refund, replay and currency-isolation rules. No casino games or premium currency are enabled in this release.

Alpha 1.4.0 (the Fourfold Chronicle)

  • Meet the people behind the diaries: Mara Fen, Dain, Hessa and Selen now live in Lanternhold’s open southern plaza. Approach and speak to them for optional conversations about the lives the crystals protect.
  • Sixteen conversations to uncover: Ask about shelter, promises, shared warmth and the freedom to choose. Further topics open as you record each witness’s field evidence and complete their realm’s crystal restoration. No quest or reward is automatically claimed.
  • The world answers your work: After a crystal’s quest is turned in, its investigation landmarks show new growth, renewed crossing cloths and ripples, warm hearths and pottery, or wind-filled pennants. These personal changes preserve the old ruins, open walking routes and shared-world hazards.
  • After the Vigil: Four new journal epilogues explain what restoration means to the people of each realm. Open pages and dialogue topics stay put during quest updates, with readable phone controls.
  • Ilyra still guides the Chronicle: The existing eight investigations, manual quest handoffs, four dungeon roads, full raid and crystal-defense requirements, resonance portal and Dark King conclusion remain intact. Witnesses are not daily quest givers, and existing progress and rewards are preserved.

Alpha 1.3.0 (combat with impact)

  • Aim with your thumb: Drag the phone skill button or an assigned hotbar skill to preview direction and range, then release to cast. Slide back to cancel. Taps keep selected-target behavior; self and ally skills keep their own targeting.
  • Reliable self buffs: Caster-centered skills and personal buffs no longer try to approach a selected enemy or turn toward the cursor before casting. Aimed charges and ally-targeted heals retain their targeting rules.
  • Know when you can cast: The target card shows cooldown or missing mana while keeping range and safe-zone warnings first. Failed casts explain the wait or exact mana shortage.
  • Feel each class: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard and Cleric have distinct local cast sounds and refined attack windup and follow-through. Short actions blend in faster without changing attack speed or damage timing.
  • Your camera, your comfort: Optional camera impacts respond to your direct combat hits and landings, not other players jumping. Adjust saved impact strength from zero to full; motion stays off by default and respects device reduced-motion settings.
  • Warnings that stand out: Dark-backed danger edges stay readable on bright ground at both graphics settings, with the same damage boundary. Nearby party hit effects are more compact without reducing your effects or hazard warnings.
  • Combat rules stay grounded: Existing server targeting, dungeon wall checks, cooldowns, mana costs, gear stats and rewards remain in force. No level-based stat multiplier has been added.

Alpha 1.2.0 (heroes worth looking at)

  • Hero refinement: Smoother exposed faces and visible hands improve the four-class models. Hands remain in place when gloves and weapons change.
  • Natural strides: Heroes lean forward when running, with smoother walking and running motion and articulated boots. Equipped footwear follows the same ankle motion. Movement speed and attack timing are unchanged.
  • Controls for your hands: Phone settings now offer left- or right-handed combat controls and independently saved touch sizing. Camera framing follows the layout; very short landscape screens keep standard control size to preserve viewing space.
  • Your camera, remembered: Phone and desktop camera zoom save independently of each other and of menu text size.
  • A readable Forge: Phone equipment lists show names, level and potency in large rows, with larger controls and collapsible forging help. Selected equipment continues to refresh after upgrades.
  • A clearer Trading House: Named inventory rows show quantities and selection. Phone selling forms and auction controls are larger, and expandable item details work without hovering.
  • Community on your phone: Social, friend and guild lists use readable cards. Guild management actions sit under Manage, and PvP challenges, results and leaderboards have readable text and touch-sized controls.
  • Explore the map by touch: Drag to pan, pinch to zoom, or use the zoom and Find me buttons. Phone labels remain readable as you zoom, and the map fits portrait and landscape screens.
